pictures.caption: Figure 1: Visualization of self-reenactment and cross-reenactment examples for each avatar generator and dataset. Left 4 columns correspond to examples for a RAVDESS [21] video, right 4 columns correspond to the examples for a CREMA-D [20] video. Top row shows the frames from the two original videos used as driving videos for the avatars. f indicates the frame number shown from the corresponding video.

Figure 2: Public avatar fingerprinting system based on a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) model [12]. From an avatar video, first the landmarks are obtained for each of the frames, and using them as input, the GCN obtains a graph embedding for each of the frames. Finally a pooling block generates a final embedding for the video from the individual graph embeddings.

Figure 4: Graphical representation of the video-to-video scoring process for an enrollmenttest pair of avatar videos. For each video, a set of fixed-length windows is computed. Since the length of the videos can be different, the number of windows for both videos X and Y can also be different. The avatar fingerprinting system generates one embedding z per window. The similarity matrix sx,y between the embeddings from all windows is computed and the final similarity score S(V e , V t ) is obtained by averaging all similarities.

Figure 5: Intra-dataset intra-generator t-SNE embedding visualizations. All obtained from CREMA-D test avatar videos generated with LivePortrait [23] generator. Left: embeddings obtained with Graph-based system. Right: embeddings obtained with DINOv2 system. Colors indicate the driving identity and marker types indicate the target identity.

tables.caption: Table 1: Summary of the curated source datasets used to generate the avatar videos.

Table 2: Statistics of AVAPrintDB. It includes soft-biometric information about the driving identity in the videos from the evaluation split. The same avatar videos are generated for each of the three avatar generators (GAGAvatar [22], LivePortrait [23], and HunyuanPortrait [24]). "Self" correspond to self-reenactments (genuine avatar) and "cross" correspond to cross-reenactments (impostor avatar).

Table 3: Soft-biometrics distribution of evaluation split of AVAPrintDB. It shows soft-biometric information about the driving identity in the evaluation split videos. The same avatar videos are generated for each of the three avatar generators (GAGAvatar [22], LivePortrait [23], and HunyuanPortrait [24]). "Self" corresponds to self-reenactments (genuine avatar) and "cross" corresponds to cross-reenactments (impostor avatar).
Table 4: Number of genuine and impostor pairs provided in our AVAPrintDB benchmark.

Table 5: Intra-dataset and intra-generator scenario. Performance in terms of AUC (%). Best result is highlighted in bold. Results are reported for each avatar generator: GAGA (GAGAvatar [22]), LIVE (LivePortrait [23]) and HUNY (HunyuanPortrait [24]).

Table 6: Intra-dataset, cross-generator scenario. Reference experiments (intragenerator) are highlighted in bold. Results are shown in AUC (%) for the reference experiments, and in ∆AUC (percentage points) with respect to the corresponding reference experiment for each cross-generator case. A positive deviation means improvement with respect to the reference experiment.

Table 7: Cross-dataset, intra-generator scenario. Reference experiments (intradataset) are highlighted in bold. Results are shown in AUC (%) for the reference experiments, and in ∆AUC (percentage points) with respect to the corresponding reference experiment for each cross-dataset case. A positive deviation means improvement with respect to the reference experiment.

Table 8: Fairness analysis of the avatar fingerprinting models for CREMA-D avatars. Results are shown in AUC (%). Performance is reported for the intra-dataset and intra-generator scenario across demographic subgroups (gender, ethnicity, and age).

Table 9: Fairness analysis of the avatar fingerprinting models for RAVDESS avatars. Results are shown in AUC (%). Performance is reported for the intra-dataset and intra-generator scenario across demographic subgroups (gender, ethnicity, and age).
